A stable remittance ratio exists; its meaning remains unknown

Report an error

01What does this evidence establish?

Over 2021–2024, the ratio of the remittance series in the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) Annual Report 2025 to the IMF 2025 Article IV series is 1.838 in every year, and the two growth paths are almost identical when indexed to 2021 = 100. The public evidence does not establish what that ratio represents, so it is a numerical regularity with no documented explanation, not a conversion rule.

02What does it measure?

The ratio of the CBY-Aden remittance series to the IMF remittance series in each year from 2021 to 2024.

03Who or what does it apply to?

The CBY-Aden publication scope compared with the IMF's analytical scope for areas under the internationally recognized government

04How current is it?

The ratio covers 2021 to 2024, from the CBY-Aden Annual Report 2025 and the IMF 2025 Article IV consultation. It should not be read as holding for later years unless newer comparable editions of both series are published.

05What this evidence does not establish

The 1.838 ratio is not a population, geography, informal-share or coverage conversion.

Limits of the measure

Comparability is component-specific only; differences of sign, scope and method remain material.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Computed by this resource from published values: the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) Annual Report 2025 remittance series (2,900.22; 3,066.58; 3,240.46; 3,422.16 US$ million for 2021–2024) and the IMF 2025 Article IV staff-report series (1,577.7; 1,668.2; 1,762.8; 1,861.7 US$ million). For each year the CBY-Aden value is divided by the IMF value; the result is 1.838 in each year. The statistical annex of the IMF 2025 Article IV consultation (Annex IV) documents the method context.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How can I verify it?

This record is drawn from the source(s) listed on this page. Open a source record to reach the original document, and check that the definition, period, population and geography match what is stated here.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
